intent: A river journey in reverse: the count that beats Egypt, the kings who ruled Egypt, then the long Nile road from the forgotten pyramids to the famous ones.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: Where are MOST of the world's pyramids?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: Where are most of the world's pyramids?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat

lines.text: Sudan. The Kingdom of Kush built more than 200 pyramids along the Nile, nearly twice Egypt's count.

lines.direction: tighten on Sudan; the Egypt counter runs to 138 on 'Egypt' while the Egyptian flag-ball thinks; a pyramid sticker on 'steeper'; the Meroe pin and tag drop on 'Meroe'
lines.text: Egypt has about 138. Sudan's are steeper and slimmer, up to 30 metres, and most stand at Meroe.

lines.direction: ease north so Sudan and Egypt share the frame; a crown sticker on 'copycat'; the 744 BC card on 'ruled'; Sudan pulses on 'century'; the Sudanese flag-ball grins
lines.text: Kush was no copycat. From 744 BC its kings ruled Egypt itself as pharaohs, for nearly a century.

lines.direction: pull out to the whole Nile; the Khartoum pin on 'Khartoum'; a camel sticker travels the river line from Meroe to Giza until 'Giza'; the Giza pin and tag land; the river sticker pulses at the end
lines.text: Meroe lies 200 kilometres north of Khartoum, and 1600 kilometres up the Nile from Giza.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
